title: roboRIO
summary: Status lights, unrecoverable errors, microSD card, imaging, USB and Ethernet reachability.

start.question: Look at the roboRIO lights. What do you see?
start.help: Lights from left: Power, Status, Radio (unused), Comm, Mode, RSL.

options.label: Comm light off, DS cannot see the robot
Comm green but robot will not move

no-power.title: roboRIO has no power
steps: Confirm the robot main breaker is on and the PDH or PDP shows a status light.
Tug the RIO power Weidmuller plug. Pull the wires out, strip fresh copper, and push them back in until they lock.
Check the RIO channel on the PDH or PDP. Reseat the fuse or breaker. A red channel LED on the PDH means no output.
Measure 12 V at the RIO plug with a meter. If there is 12 V and no lights, the RIO is dead.
Swap the roboRIO, image it, and set the team number.

power-color.question: Is the Power light amber or red?

brownout.title: Amber Power light: brownout protection tripped
steps: Read the battery voltage in the DS. Under 12.3 V at rest means a weak battery. Swap it for a fully charged one.
Check the DS log for voltage dips below 6.8 V when motors start. That is a brownout. Lower motor supply current limits, drive first.
Wiggle the battery connector and the main breaker lugs. Try to rotate each lug by hand. If it turns, tighten the nut.
Check the RIO power wires are on their own PDH or PDP channel, not shared with the radio or a motor.
Use the Power guide in this app for limits and breaker checks, and look at the DS log with the team.

rail-short.title: Red Power light: short on a user rail
steps: Power off. Unplug everything from the RIO DIO, PWM, analog, and the 5 V and 6 V rails.
Power on with nothing connected. If the light is green now, plug devices back one at a time to find the short.
Look for a stray wire strand or a metal chip touching the RIO pins. Clean it out.
Check any sensor cable with a crushed or pinched jacket.
If the light is red with nothing plugged in, the RIO is damaged. Swap it.

which-rio.question: Which roboRIO is it?
which-rio.help: roboRIO 2 has a microSD card slot on the side and a 2.0 label. roboRIO 1 has no card slot.

rio2-status.question: How is the Status light blinking?

options.label: Flashing all the time, never pauses
Groups of 2, 3, or 4 flashes, then a pause
Stays on solid after a minute

rio1-status.question: How is the Status light blinking?

options.label: Stays on solid after a minute

rio2-unrecoverable.title: roboRIO 2 unrecoverable error: continuous flashing
steps: On a roboRIO 2 a Status light that flashes without pausing means it cannot boot from the microSD card.
Power off. Pull the microSD card. Look in the slot with a light for metal chips or debris. Blow it out with air. Reseat the card until it clicks.
Power on and wait 60 seconds. If it still flashes, reimage the card on a laptop with the roboRIO 2 image (balenaEtcher or Raspberry Pi Imager), then set the team number with the Imaging Tool.
If reimaging does not fix it, try a different microSD card. Cards fail.
Still flashing with a fresh card: swap the roboRIO. Repeated unrecoverable errors on the same unit have been debris in the slot.

links.label: NI forum: RIO 2 stuck in unrecoverable error

rio1-unrecoverable.title: roboRIO 1 unrecoverable error: 4 flashes then a pause
steps: On a roboRIO 1, 4 flashes then a pause means the software crashed twice without a reboot.
Press the reset button once. Wait 60 seconds.
If it repeats, hold reset for at least 5 seconds to boot into Safe Mode. Connect by USB and reimage with the roboRIO Imaging Tool (Format Target).
Check the RIO power wiring. Repeated crashes at power on can be a loose Weidmuller on the RIO plug.
If it will not image or keeps crashing, swap the roboRIO.

blink-codes.title: Status blink codes: 2, 3, or 4 flashes
steps: 2 flashes: software error. Reimage the roboRIO.
3 flashes: Safe Mode. Press reset once. If it comes back in Safe Mode, reimage.
4 flashes on a roboRIO 2: software crashed twice. Reboot. Reimage if it repeats.
Before reimaging a roboRIO 2, reseat the microSD card and check the slot for debris.
After reimaging, set the team number and redeploy code. Walk the team through it if they have never imaged a RIO.

reach.question: Can the laptop reach the RIO at all?
reach.help: Test over USB first. Plug a USB A to B cable into the RIO and open http://172.22.11.2/ in a browser.

options.label: Yes over USB, no over Ethernet
Not tested yet, only tried the network

reach-network.title: Check the network path to the RIO
steps: From the DS laptop open a command prompt. Run ping 10.TE.AM.2 (team 1234 is 10.12.34.2). A reply means the network is fine and the DS setup is the problem.
No reply: check the RIO Ethernet cable is in the radio RIO port and both ends show link lights.
Turn off Wi-Fi and disable every adapter except the one connected to the radio. Set that adapter to DHCP.
Turn off the Windows firewall. Open the DS Diagnostics tab and check the Robot Radio and Robot ping lights.
If the radio pings (10.TE.AM.1) but the RIO does not, plug into the RIO by USB and go back to this question.

ethernet-dead.title: RIO works over USB but not Ethernet
steps: On the RIO web page over USB, check the Ethernet interface has an address. 10.TE.AM.2 through the radio, 169.254.x.x on a direct cable, or blank means no link.
Swap the Ethernet cable. Try the other radio port for a moment to prove the cable and radio are fine, then move it back to the RIO port.
Look at the RIO port for bent pins or a broken latch tab on the plug.

If the port is dead, plug a USB Ethernet adapter into the RIO USB A port and run the radio cable to it. The RIO picks it up as a second network interface. This has got a robot through an event with a dead port.
Swap the roboRIO when there is a spare. Tell the team to contact NI for a repair.

links.label: NI KB: Ethernet port not working on roboRIO

usb-dead.title: RIO does not answer over USB or Ethernet
steps: Try a different USB cable and a different laptop USB port. Make sure NI FRC Game Tools is installed so the USB driver exists.
Hold the reset button for at least 5 seconds to enter Safe Mode, then try the Imaging Tool over USB.
Ask if anything USB was unplugged or plugged on the robot. Unshielded USB extension cables have carried static that killed both RIO USB ports. Remove extensions and try the built-in ports again.
Check the Status light. If it flashes without pause, follow the unrecoverable error branch of this guide.
If Safe Mode does not respond either, the RIO needs replacing. Swap it.

comm-red.question: Is the Comm light solid red or blinking red?

no-code.title: Solid red Comm: DS connected, no user code running
steps: In the DS click Restart Robot Code and wait 15 seconds.
Read the DS Console. A stack trace at start means the code crashed. Fix that first.
Check the WPILib year of the code matches the RIO image year. A mismatch never runs.
Reboot the RIO. If code still does not start, redeploy from the team laptop.
Use the Code and deploy guide in this app if the team cannot find the crash.

estop.title: Blinking red Comm: E-stop is active
steps: An E-stop stays latched until the roboRIO reboots.
On the field, the head referee or FTA clears it. Do not touch the field E-stop button.
In the pit, check nobody pressed Space in the DS. Reboot the RIO to clear it.
If it E-stops again with nobody touching the DS, look for a stuck key or a joystick mapped to the E-stop.

wont-move.title: Comm green, code running, robot will not move
steps: Check the Mode light. Off means disabled or brownout. Enable from the DS and watch it turn green (teleop) or orange (auto).
Check the RSL is on. A blinking RSL means enabled. No RSL means the robot is disabled or the RSL has no power.
Check the DS Joysticks light is green. Press F1 to rescan. Confirm the controller is in the USB slot the code expects.
Watch the battery voltage when enabling. A drop under 6.8 V disables outputs. Swap the battery.
If motors still do nothing, check the CAN bus. Use the CAN guide in this app.
